fact: INSA, with its Director General speaking, is stated on 29 September 2026 to co-chair a newly established Financial Sector Cybersecurity Forum with the National Bank of Ethiopia, for threat sharing and coordinated incident response.

INSA is stated to be the national body under Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity Proclamation No. 1426/2026, which sets the foundation for cybersecurity monitoring and coordinated incident response; the document gives no proclamation date, so the publication date is used.

The proclamation identifies 12 critical infrastructure sectors (ICT, finance, transport, health, energy and others) and requires owners and operators to meet 18 cybersecurity obligations; the document gives no enactment date, so the publication date is used.

A National Computer Emergency Response Team is stated to exist as the body receiving incident reports under the newly enacted Proclamation No. 1426/2026, alongside INSA; the document gives no enactment date, so the publication date is used.

Proclamation No. 1426/2026 identifies 12 critical infrastructure sectors and requires their owners and operators to report cyber incidents to the National CERT within 48 hours, among 18 obligations; the publication date is used as no enactment date is given.
The 2026/27 federal budget appropriates ETB 3,108,049,744 to INSA, described as the national information- and network-security agency and the state's central cyber-security institution.
The 2025/26 federal budget appropriates ETB 2,502,115,991 to INSA, described as the national information- and network-security agency and the state's central cyber-security institution.

The Ministry of Finance record states INSA is Ethiopia's national information- and network-security agency, appropriated ETB 1,600,000,000 for 2024/25 with cyber programmes (Information Assurance, National Cyber Capabilities), so it exists and operates; as_of is the appropriation date.

Fana reports INSA is recognised on the Day of Resilience for its efforts to counter cyberattacks targeting the country, stating it operates as a national cyber body; no specific incident or alert is given.

The 2026/27 federal budget record states INSA runs the Information Assurance cyber-security programme, appropriated ETB 579,480,309 (recurrent 305,173,709, capital 274,306,600); as_of is the appropriation date.
INSA issued Directive No. 1135/2026 on IT products security clearance and control in May 2026, showing the body exists and operates; the directive concerns product clearance, not incident response.

The 2025/26 federal budget appropriated ETB 584,832,316 (recurrent 184,832,316, capital 400,000,000) to INSA's Information Assurance programme, described as the cyber-security programme of the national information-network-security agency.

The 2024/25 executive budget proposal (proposed, not appropriated) put ETB 450,145,000 to INSA's Information Assurance programme, described as the cyber-security programme of the national information-network-security agency.

The story has the INSA Director General speaking on cybersecurity foundations laid under Digital Ethiopia 2025 and cybersecurity as a priority under DE2030, showing INSA operating as the national cyber body; dated by the launch on 2025-12-21.

fact: INSA Director General Tigist Hamid said Ethio-CERT had identified, responded to and reported more than 71,000 cyberattacks in 2018 E.C.

Digital Policy Alert states that INSA reported in October 2024 that it addressed approximately 8,854 data breach cases.

INSA said it thwarted 98.56 percent of 4,623 attempted cyberattacks on government and private institutions in the past six months of the Ethiopian fiscal year.
INSA director-general reported 4,623 attempted cyberattacks in the half year, up 115 percent on the same period a year earlier.
